The Battle of Liegnitz (German:Schlacht bei Liegnitz, Polish:Bitwa pod Legnicą) was a engagement during the Thirty Years' War, the resulting action was between an Imperial army under the command of  and a Saxon Army under Hans Georg von Arnim-Boitzenburg.  The battle took place at Liegnitz and was a Saxon victory, following the battle Arnim overran Silesia while Johan Banér invaded Bohemia.
Prelude
In March of 1618, a group of Czech Protestant Nobels threw out their Catholic Administrators, this snowball into the Thirty Years' War.  During the Bohemian Revolt the Protestant Johann Georg I, Elector of Saxony would side with the Catholic Ferdinand von Habsburg in exchange for the session of Lusatia.
Frederick von Wittelsbach, Count Palatine was defeated by the Catholic Liga at White Mountain but the fighting continued in Frederick's German territories.  The Danes would intervene in 1625 but withdrew in 1627.
In 1630 Swedish King, Gustavus Adolphus, landed on Wollin and soon overran Pomerania, Brandenburg-Prussia, Ducal Saxony, and Mecklenburg.  Johann Georg would make alliance with Gustavus and would win a major victory at Breitenfeld.  Johann Georg would hire the German General, Hans Georg von Arnim-Boitzenburg, who would invade Silesia with support form the Swedish-Scottish General Jacob Duwall.  Arnim would win a victory over Don Baltasar Marradas at Steinau and occupied Silesia.  In 1632 Albrecht von Wallenstein retook Silesia after the Second Battle of Steinau, Duwall would escape capture and form a partisan band.
Johann Georg desired Silesia to be his own territory so he sent an army under Arnim threw Lusatia and into Lower Silesia, Arnim stopped at Goldberg.  The Imperial Commander in the region was  who had between 19,200-22,000 and moved to meet Arnim at Leignitz.
Strength
Colloredo had between 19,200-22,000 with  around 11,200 cavalry and 8,000 infantry and 13 cavalry regiments and 3 infantry regiments.  Arnim had an unknown amount of men but had 8 cavalry regiments and 5 infantry regiments.
Battle
On the night of may 13, Arnim and the Saxony army set off form Goldberg to follow Colloredo to Liegnitz.  As soon as the Imperial's noticed Arnim's vanguard, the formal advanced in full battle order against the cavalry.
Before the battle begun Arnim, following Gustavus Adolphus's practice, sung a verse.  Following this Arnim gathered his colonels and communicated his plan to them, and then attacked the Imperials, who in turn attacked the Saxon vanguard.  A mutual exchange of cannon fire proved detrimental to the Saxons.
As soon as the Imperial's noticed Arnim's vanguard, the formal advanced in full battle order against the cavalry. Arnim feared that despondency among his men and therefore, under the battle cry "God is our help", ordered his entire battle line into an advance.  Cavalry detachments on the Saxon side wings attacked both wings of the Imperial army with two 300 strong corps on both flanks, while the infantry attacked in the front.  The Imperial line stood firm and threw the Saxons back.
Arnim brought up new regiments, which now succeeded in routing the Imperials; but Colloredo brought up his reserve forward, thereby halting his own troops again, whereupon both sides engaged in bloody melee.  Finally, the Saxons advanced again, and the Imperial left began retreating.
Then generals  and  broke the Imperial cavalry, and the flight of the Imperial cavalry spread to the infantry who also began the flee to Lienis.
Colloredo tried to restore the situation with a counter attck against the right wing but was unsuccessful, and they now retreated.
According to E. O. Schmidt, the Saxons lost 1,000 dead or wounded, while the Imperials lost 4,000 dead, 1,400 captured, and 95 flag.
Aftermath
Casualties
The Imperials lost 3,000 killed, 1,400 captured, and 28 colors, 12 standards, 8 cannons, and all of their ammunition, while the Saxons lost 400 dead, according to Carl Du Jarrys de la Roche.
Following the battle, Colloredo withdrew back to Glaß with his remaining troops, without being pursued by Arnim, who turned to Breslau.  He now met up with Jacob Duwall's partisans, but conflict lead to both armies not cooperating, but not long after Duwall died.  The conflict between the Swedes and Saxons would be saved when Swedish General Johan Banér, who moved south having successfully besieged Frankfurt an Der Oder.
Banér moved south linking up with Arnim at Großglogau, which had been captured by Banér.  Following the siege, Banér remained with the Swedes at Neuensalz.  Banér marched south to Zittau where Johann Georg Elector of Saxony had left a small force to drive out the Croats.
Banér moved south into Northern Bohemia, where he crossed the Elbe, and now he moved south, with the support of Johann Georg, and then onto Prague which he captured.  Upon hearing the news of the Swedish Defeat at Nördlingen, Banér abandoned Bohemia and retread to the Swedish Bridgehead.
